basis: Lens dislocation defines disease; supplied annotations report joint stiffness in 80-99% and cognitive impairment in 30-79%, supporting joint and neurologic dysfunction.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration with pyramidal and sensory dysfunction; abnormal saccades are neurologic rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Tongue and oral malformations plus limb reduction define the syndrome; structural fingernail abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Intellectual disability is under 30%.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm production and morphology; reproductive dysfunction without evidence of endocrine disease.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; scoliosis and fixed flexion contractures each reported in 1/1 support structural musculoskeletal involvement, with limited frequency evidence.
The syndrome is defined by progressive dilated cardiomyopathy and childhood sensorineural hearing loss, both reported in 80-99%.
Parathyroid hyperfunction secondary to established renal dysfunction defines this renal-endocrine disorder; renal osteodystrophy is a separately specified manifestation.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy with characteristic opacities and microcysts; no systemic organ involvement established.
Metabolic neurodegeneration with rhabdomyolysis (13/15); cardiac conduction disease in 8/13. GI dysmotility (30-79%) omitted by cap; transaminases alone do not establish liver damage.
Noonan cardiac phenotype; prolonged PT in 2/2, keratosis pilaris in 3/5 and developmental delay in 2/5 support coagulation, skin and neurologic involvement; small cohort.
Autoinflammation with marrow disease; pulmonary infiltrates 72% and inflammatory skin lesions ~80%. Auricular chondritis 64% and vascular thrombosis 44% omitted by cap.
Suppurative infection of the intracranial or spinal subdural space directly affects the central nervous system.
Tuberculous infection involving brain, spinal cord or meninges; pulmonary tuberculosis is a separately specified disease site.
Inherited lysine-catabolism defect; developmental delay reported in 2/2 supports neurologic involvement, although penetrance is uncertain. Aciduria alone is not renal damage.
Defined by alopecia, progressive sensorineural deafness and endocrine hypogonadism with LH and GH deficiencies.
Inherited proximal tubular disease with nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, proteinuria and progressive renal failure; hypercalciuria reflects renal dysfunction.
Persistent dyskeratotic plaques of conjunctival and oral epithelium define the disease; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
EBV-driven B-cell neoplasm centered in lungs; CNS lesions occur in ~30-40%. Skin involvement ~30-50% omitted by cap; renal involvement is generally below 30%.
Malignant B-cell lymphoma arising in the colon or rectum; gastrointestinal origin and lymphoid-cell and lymphoma mechanisms define the axes.
Genetic podocyte disease causing glomerulosclerosis, proteinuria and renal failure; an immune mechanism is not established for TRPC6-associated disease.
Epidermal nevi with phosphate-wasting, vitamin D-resistant rickets define a cutaneous, metabolic and skeletal syndrome; phosphate wasting alone does not establish kidney damage.
Soft-tissue sarcoma with skeletal-muscle differentiation; paratesticular and head-and-neck locations do not establish damage to additional organ axes.
Interstitial lung injury caused by drug or radiation exposure; pulmonary damage defines this disease despite its treatment-related cause.
Congenital malformations of cardiac outflow tracts and great arteries; associated syndromes do not establish additional organ involvement across this group.
Metaplastic lesion located in urethral urothelium; the renal axis includes the urethra. The name does not imply a separate kidney lesion.
